decisions.reason: The candidate applies to standalone operation of the modular main board. The source establishes integrated-board charging and rail needs but does not change the modular standalone USB supply.
The source does not address battery-connector placement, orientation, spacing, or mounting-hole clearance on the modular power board.
The source concerns an integrated single-board redesign and does not cancel or revise the existing interface requirements within their modular-board contexts.
The source changes power-path needs for an integrated board but does not revise the mechanical layout of the modular power board.
Requiring a 5V rail does not necessarily change the existing GPIO-switched sensor rail, its converter, loads, or control behavior.
The source does not address the panel-mounted power button, its connector, or its PWRON signal connection.
The requirement to provide 3.3V and 5V rails does not alter whether or how those rails are monitored.

The integrated-board redesign may eliminate the modular Schottky-drop condition that justified a 3.4V DCDC1 output, but the source neither confirms the integrated topology nor specifies a revised output voltage.
The invitation to suggest a simpler power solution is consistent with the existing cost-conscious integrated-board policy and establishes no new sourcing constraint.
The source establishes integrated-board power capabilities but does not change any sensor-module connector, pinout, or interface requirement.
AXP2101 alternatives are only invited for consideration; no replacement is selected and no thermal-pad requirement is changed.
The source discusses charging during operation but does not resolve or modify the battery connector series, pinout, or mounting type.
